symptom: `mxcli mcp capabilities -p App.mpr --mcp http://localhost:7782/mcp` on Windows failed with `dial tcp <LAN IP>:7782: i/o timeout`, still after the host.docker.internal fix; `--mcp-dial 127.0.0.1:7782` connected. The same report said `exec --mcp` / `-c --mcp` wrote the .mpr and mprcontents/ and skipped the .mpr.lock refusal (mendixlabs/mxcli#1684)
cause: dialPlan dialled the URL host verbatim, so `localhost` went through the resolver, which on the reporter's machine answered with a LAN address first; Studio Pro on Windows listens on 127.0.0.1 only and answers 400 to any Host header but localhost. The write-to-disk claim does not reproduce: the CLI with --mcp sends ped_create_document and leaves .mpr + mprcontents/ byte-identical with the lock present, and an un-routed statement is refused by the MCP backend's unsupportedBackend; the trace that showed no PED call was the tracer wiring fixed earlier (2026-11-01-mcp-trace-lists-no-ped-call)
fix: A localhost endpoint dials 127.0.0.1:<port> first, then localhost:<port> via the resolver (a ::1-only server), then host.docker.internal; the request URL, and so the Host header, stays localhost
insight: Before fixing 'writes the file instead of the server', run the real binary with the reporter's exact flags against a logging fake server and a hash of the model files, with the lock file present: one run separated what the server received from what the trace printed. Pin it with a child-process test (runMainStreams) and prove the test by forcing the fault back in (factory ignoring --mcp plus the guard off), which reproduces the report verbatim: exit 0, `Created constant`, no PED call, files changed. Do not 'restore' the lock refusal for --mcp: it guards the local Writer, which the MCP backend never opens (ConnectReadOnly); with --mcp the lock is always present, so refusing on it would make --mcp unusable
